html:
The Bibulman are an Aboriginal people of the far southwest of Western Australia, in the tall forest country around the south coast between Augusta and the lower Warren and Frankland rivers. They are one of the fourteen language groups of the Noongar.

Their neighbours were the Wardandi to the west, the Kaniyang inland and the Minang to the east around King George Sound. Like other Noongar, they moved through their country with the seasons, fishing the inlets and rivers in summer and burning the bush in a planned way to keep it open for game.

British settlement reached the southwest after the founding of the Swan River Colony in 1829, and farms and timber cutting spread into Bibulman country through the 1800s. The Bibbulmun Track, a long walking trail from Perth to Albany, is named after them. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815, before the colony arrived. Their wider history is told in Aboriginal Australian societies.
